subject.title: perf: avoid event-loop stall during embedded_run bootstrap-context

question: Should OpenClaw accept this custom yielding glob walker and bootstrap-hook scheduling as the bounded fix for bootstrap-context event-loop stalls despite possible prompt-ordering and session-timing changes?
rationale: The patch is correct and well-proven for the targeted hot path, but bootstrap file selection, ordering, and hook scheduling are compatibility-sensitive context surfaces whose upgrade tradeoff requires owner intent.

options.title: Land After Exact-Head Verification
options.body: Accept the internal compatibility tradeoff, rebase onto current main, and merge after exact-head checks and focused bootstrap parity tests pass.

options.title: Require Live Channel Proof
options.body: Keep the implementation but require a current-head embedded-run or channel-latency transcript showing channel I/O remains responsive during bootstrap.

options.title: Pause For Broader Runtime Design
options.body: Hold or close this PR if maintainers prefer worker isolation, priority scheduling, or caching instead of owning a custom glob implementation.

recommendation.title: Land After Exact-Head Verification
recommendation.body: Accept the internal compatibility tradeoff, rebase onto current main, and merge after exact-head checks and focused bootstrap parity tests pass.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history across internal hooks, bootstrap hook architecture, and boundary-safe workspace reads places the compatibility decision in this ownership area.
